key_insight: A Transformer model trained on routine blood tests and diagnosis histories can identify people at elevated pancreatic cancer risk up to 3 years before diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could help enrich screening populations for pancreatic cancer, making targeted surveillance and earlier curative-intent treatment more feasible.
method: Longitudinal coded diagnoses and blood test trajectories were used as model inputs.
A custom Transformer with multi-head attention predicted future pancreatic cancer risk.
External validation used leave-one-site-out testing at 1, 2, and 3 years before diagnosis.
evidence_signal: In external validation, AUROC was 0.837 at 1 year, 0.797 at 2 years, and 0.760 at 3 years, with good calibration and a Brier score of 0.025.
watch_item: Implementation will need careful prospective validation across real-world settings to confirm transportability, threshold performance, and equitable impact.
paper_title: Digitally enriching a screening population for pancreatic cancer using routine blood-based measures and clinical histories
